title: Drones Offer Central Asia an Escape From Foreign Dependency
author: Michael S. Coffey
text:
A Turkish Baykar Bayraktar TB2
Credit: Wikimedia Commons / Bayhaluk
Drones are everywhere in the news and on the frontlines of the Iran-U.S. War and the Russia-Ukraine War, but their most recent use on a battlefield in Central Asia represents a long-term issue – continued dependency on foreign suppliers. The Central Asian states may just be replacing their long-term Russian security dependency with a Turkish one.Central Asian leaders risk deepening this dependency and worsening security vulnerabilities as they announce deals with foreign suppliers that are often headquartered in a single state – Turkiye. However, developments in 2026 show that opportunities for local development and production that would benefit regional economies without offloading security responsibilities exist. Local politicians just need to invest locally.[...]
